voice: 温暖自然英式女老师｜IndexTTS2.5 慢速教学

chunks.text: Wukong, Tiangong, Tianwen ... Do you know where the names of Chinese space programmes come from?
The well-known moon mission Chang'e is named after a goddess who flew to the moon.
This mission was important in studying the moon's surface.
Wukong, the dark matter particle explorer, is named after a Chinese superhero, Monkey King.
According to Journey to the West,
Monkey King has a pair of sharp eyes which can tell the difference between good and evil.
The Wukong satellite is just as sharp-eyed as Monkey King to help scientists search for dark matter in space.
The name of the space station, Tiangong, means 'Heavenly Palace'.
In Chinese myths, this is the home of Tian Di.
Now, Tiangong Space Station is a home for Chinese astronauts in space.
Tianwen, China's Mars mission, gets its name from the poem Tianwen by Qu Yuan.
Qu Yuan is a well-known poet from ancient China.
In Tianwen, he had questions about the sky, stars, nature, myths and the real world, showing his hunger for truth.
Perhaps the Tianwen missions will end up answering some of Qu Yuan's questions.
If you look into more names of Chinese space programmes, you will find that they all have beautiful meanings.
We, the Chinese people, have a long-cherished space dream.
Therefore, the naming of Chinese space programmes is taken very seriously.
Scientists, from junior members to experienced leaders,
are also working hard to sweep away setbacks,
without letting any challenges disappoint them.
The names are like postcards to the world, showing our determination in space exploration.
